strategies.name: vwap_20sma_long_pullback_trend_scalp
strategies.entry_summary: On the 2-minute chart, get bullish once price closes over both VWAP and the 20 SMA, then enter long on a following candle confirming that strength or on pullbacks/bounces that retest VWAP while price continues to hold above VWAP and the 20 SMA. Additional buy entries can be taken on repeated VWAP b-
strategies.exit_summary: For a quick scalp, take profits into the upper VWAP band. For a longer hold, stay in the trade while VWAP and the 20 SMA trend higher, then use the 20 SMA as a trailing stop and exit on a close below the 20 SMA once price has separated from VWAP.

variants.variant_label: quick scalp to VWAP upper band
variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: enter after close above VWAP and 20 SMA, or on bounce/retest of VWAP while holding above it
variants.target_note: take profits into the upper VWAP channel/band
variants.transcript_quote: you can throw the upper and lower channels on the vwap... and you can sell for profits into the upper Channel

variants.variant_label: extended hold with 20 SMA trailing stop
variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: keep buying/holding VWAP tests that do not close below VWAP
variants.target_note: hold while VWAP and 20 SMA trend higher; exit on close below 20 SMA as trailing stop
variants.transcript_quote: you can use the 20 SMA as a trailing stop so if we do close below the 20 SMA maybe you can use that as an indication to get out of the trade

strategies.name: vwap_20sma_short_rejection_after_bearish_break
strategies.entry_summary: If price loses VWAP and the 20 SMA together, closes below VWAP, and a following candle starts to build below, stop looking to buy the bounce and instead short the rejection of VWAP and the 20 SMA.
strategies.exit_summary: Exit logic is not concretely taught beyond the short entry/rejection idea; no runnable stop, target, or repeatable management rule is provided for the short.

result.enumeration_note: The video clearly teaches one runnable long VWAP+20 SMA pullback strategy with two compatible management variants (quick band target vs longer trailing-stop hold). The bearish short is mentioned as an opposite idea, but its exit/management is not taught concretely enough to satisfy the evidence floor.
